schemas.name: text_2_24
schemas.content: The NIPBL gene encodes a protein forming a dimer with MAU2 as a cohesin loader complex that is essential for sister chromatid

schemas.name: text_2_25
schemas.content: cohesion, chromosome condensation, and DNA repair.

schemas.name: text_2_27
schemas.content: Defects in the NIPBL gene may cause autosomal dominant Cornelia de Lange syndrome 1 (OMIM: 122470), which is a multisystem

schemas.name: text_2_28
schemas.content: disorder characterized by growth retardation, developmental delay, intellectual disability, distinctive craniofacial features,

schemas.name: text_2_29
schemas.content: hypertrichosis, seizures (less common), ocular anomalies, hearing loss, feeding difficulties, congenital heart defects (septal defects,

schemas.name: text_2_30
schemas.content: pulmonary or peripheral pulmonary stenosis, coarctation of the aorta, tetralogy of Fallot), distal limb defects with greater involvement of

schemas.name: text_2_31
schemas.content: the upper limbs (small hands/feet, phocomelia, oligodactyly, proximally placed thumbs, clinodactyly, toe syndactyly), gastrointestinal

schemas.name: text_2_32
schemas.content: problems, genitourinary anomalies, and behavioral abnormalities such as autism and self-injurious behavior. Distinctive craniofacial

schemas.name: text_2_33
schemas.content: features may include microbrachycephaly, low anterior hairline, synophrys, arched eyebrows, long eyelashes, ptosis, short nasal

schemas.name: text_2_34
schemas.content: bridge with anteverted nares, cleft or high-arched palate, think upper lip, downturned corners of mouth, dental anomalies, and

schemas.name: text_2_39
schemas.content: The c.2479del (p.R827Gfs*20) variant in the NIPBL gene has been described as pathogenic in ClinVar (ID: 950707). This

schemas.name: text_2_40
schemas.content: variant has been previously reported as de novo in individuals with Cornelia de Lange syndrome  (PMID: 20824775, 36913886).

schemas.name: text_2_41
schemas.content: This variant has not been observed in the gnomAD v4 dataset.

schemas.name: text_2_42
schemas.content: This frameshift variant is located in exon 10 of 47 and predicted to be deleterious.

schemas.name: text_3_26
schemas.content: The KMT2D gene encodes a histone methyltransferase that methylates the lysine 4 of histone H3 (H3K4) as part of the chromatin

schemas.name: text_3_27
schemas.content: remodeling machinery involved in transcriptional regulation and DNA repair.

schemas.name: text_3_29
schemas.content: Defects in the KMT2D gene may cause autosomal dominant Kabuki syndrome 1 (OMIM: 147920), which is characterized by postnatal

schemas.name: text_3_30
schemas.content: growth restriction, developmental delay, intellectual disability, distinct facial features (long palpebral fissures, eversion of the lateral

schemas.name: text_3_31
schemas.content: third of the lower eyelids, wide-arched eyebrows, large prominent/cupped earlobes, short columella with broad/depressed nasal tip),

schemas.name: text_3_32
schemas.content: infantile hypotonia, persistence of fingertip pads, and musculoskeletal anomalies (joint hypermobility, scoliosis, brachydactyly, short

schemas.name: text_3_33
schemas.content: fifth finger). Additional clinical features may include seizures, ptosis, strabismus, ear pits, hearing loss, cleft lip/palate, widely spaced

schemas.name: text_3_34
schemas.content: teeth, hypodontia, congenital heart defects, congenital hypothyroidism, gastrointestinal and genitourinary anomalies such as anal

schemas.name: text_3_35
schemas.content: atresia and horseshoe kidneys, an increased susceptibility to infections, autoimmune disorders, and endocrinologic abnormalities

schemas.name: text_3_36
schemas.content: (hyperinsulinism, premature thelarche). Defects in the KMT2D gene may also cause autosomal dominant branchial arch abnormalities,

schemas.name: text_3_37
schemas.content: choanal atresia, athelia, hearing loss, and hypothyroidism syndrome (OMIM: 620186), which is characterized by choanal atresia,

schemas.name: text_3_38
schemas.content: athelia or hypoplastic nipples, branchial sinus abnormalities, neck pits, lacrimal duct anomalies, hearing loss, external ear

schemas.name: text_3_39
schemas.content: malformations, and thyroid abnormalities. Additional clinical features may include growth retardation, developmental delay, and

schemas.name: text_3_45

schemas.name: text_4_31
schemas.content: 31999386), which is characterized by developmental delay, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorder. Additional clinical

schemas.name: text_4_32
schemas.content: features are highly variable, including growth delay, nonspecific craniofacial dysmorphism often with macrocephaly or microcephaly,

schemas.name: text_4_33
schemas.content: epicanthal folds, and small ears, abnormal brain imaging, vision issues (strabismus, myopia, hyperopia), gastrointestinal problems,

schemas.name: text_4_34
schemas.content: congenital heart defects, and musculoskeletal anomalies. Currently, the gene-disease association between BAZ2B and

schemas.name: text_4_35
schemas.content: neurodevelopmental defects is supported by a limited number of affected individuals. Further clinical and genetic studies are

schemas.name: text_4_36
schemas.content: warranted to better define disease onset, penetrance, and genotype-phenotype correlations.
